strengths_deep_dive: While limited governance controls constrain its overall standing, Dawat-E-Islami USA directs substantial capital to program implementation. In FY2025 disclosures, the charity reported a <cite id="[1]">93.7% program expense Ratio</cite>, reflecting an operational model that minimizes traditional administrative expenses. Furthermore, the organization holds <cite id="[1]">20.2 months of working capital</cite> in reserve, which offers strong financial cushioning against short-term revenue drops.
rich_narrative.summary: Dawat-E-Islami USA operates primary programs focused on religious education, Islamic broadcasting, and community services, but faces significant governance and outcome-tracking limitations that constrain its overall evaluation. In FY2025 filings, the organization reported a <cite id="[3]">Total Revenue of $2,429,214</cite>, supported primarily by public contributions. The charity reports a <cite id="[1]">93.7% program expense Ratio</cite>, with its evaluated program ratio score based on a <cite id="[1]">93.7% program expense rate</cite>. Despite maintaining low overhead costs, the organization demonstrates severe gaps in independent board oversight and lacks third-party evaluations to verify program efficacy. While the charity maintains <cite id="[1]">20.2 months of operating reserves</cite> and accepts <cite id="[2]">zakat contributions for eligible categories</cite>, its governance structure and transparency disclosures fall short of standard benchmarks.
